name: TEXT
description: TEXT converts a number or date into text using a user-supplied format code, so the displayed value can be concatenated or presented in a custom format.
tldr: Formats a number or date as text using a format code.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric value, date, time, or cell reference to format.

parameters.name: format_text
parameters.description: A text string enclosed in quotes that specifies the number format, e.g. "0.0%" or "yyyy-mm-dd".

basicExample.description: Show a fraction as a percent
basicExample.explanation: 0.25 is formatted with one decimal of percent precision, producing the text string "25.0%".

advancedExamples.title: Format a date
advancedExamples.scenario: Building a label from a date cell A1 containing 2024-01-15
advancedExamples.description: Convert a date into a readable text label
advancedExamples.explanation: The date serial is rendered as a fixed-width text string using the year-month-day pattern.

advancedExamples.title: Thousands separator with currency
advancedExamples.description: Apply a thousands and currency format
advancedExamples.explanation: The #,##0 grouping adds thousand separators and the currency symbol is prepended.

howItWorks: TEXT takes a numeric value and applies the formatting codes from format_text (which mirror custom number formats). The result is always a text string, not a number, so it can no longer be used directly in math without conversion back via VALUE.

howToSteps.name: Pick the value
howToSteps.text: Select the number or date cell you want to format.

howToSteps.name: Choose a format code
howToSteps.text: Write the format code in double quotes, e.g. "0.00%".

limitations: The output is text, so it cannot be used directly in arithmetic without converting back with VALUE.
Format codes are locale dependent (decimal and thousands separators differ by region).
TEXT cannot reformat an already-text string; it only formats underlying numeric/date values.

commonErrors.cause: The format_text argument is missing or is not a valid text string.
commonErrors.fix: Provide a quoted format code such as "0.0%".

commonErrors.cause: Forgetting quotes around the format code turns it into a defined name or range.
commonErrors.fix: Always enclose the format code in double quotes.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TEXT works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax.

faq.question: Why does TEXT return text instead of a number?
faq.answer: Its purpose is to produce a formatted display string, so the result is text even though the input was a number.

faq.question: Can I use TEXT on a date?
faq.answer: Yes, supply a date format code such as "mm/dd/yyyy" and the underlying date serial is rendered as text.

faq.question: How do I convert the text back to a number?
faq.answer: Wrap the result with VALUE, e.g. =VALUE(TEXT(0.25,"0.0%")).
